transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-05
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Jenna Patel (Redwood CSM), Ayesha Khan (CTO), Liam O'Connor (Head ML), Jamal Brooks (Platform), Sofia Ruiz (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Kickoff for AcornField's activation and SLA intake; primary concerns: data residency (EU), SOC2, VPC/on-prem connectivity, latency targets and cost envelope.
- Agreed to pilot with hosted but VPC peering, run benchmarks, and validate SSO/KMS flow.
- Next steps around security docs, network diagram, and pilot SOW.

Topics: Onboarding scope; network and security; pilot sizing; SLA and runbook; benchmarks and acceptance criteria.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We, uh, we really appreciate you taking the time. Quick intros? I'll kick off — Maya, AE at Redwood.
[00:14] Ayesha Khan: Hi, I'm Ayesha, CTO at AcornField. We're looking to stand up inference for customer-facing features — conversational search and summary — with strict EU residency.
[00:22] Diego Ramos: Diego, Redwood SE, I'll own the technical intake and pilot benchmarks.
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: Liam, Head of ML. We'll be integrating through our pipeline, want to understand model variants and quantization options.
[00:36] Jenna Patel: Jenna, CSM, I'll be your onboarding contact.
[00:40] Jamal Brooks: Jamal, platform. I'm focused on networking, VPC, and CI/CD hooks.
[00:44] Sofia Ruiz: Sofia here, product — defining success criteria and timelines.

[01:05] Maya Chen: Great. Agenda — security and compliance handshake, connectivity options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), pilot size and SLA targets, and then action items. Any additions?
[01:12] Ayesha Khan: No, that covers it. Critical: we need SOC2 Type II evidence, and our SIEM must ingest audit logs, plus KMS for keys.
[01:21] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll attach the security pack after the call. It has SOC2 summary, encryption at rest/in transit, audit log formats, and notes on KMS/HSM integrations.

[02:05] Diego Ramos: On connectivity — for fastest path to value we usually recommend hosted with VPC peering or private endpoints. For regulated data we do Redwood Private but that requires more lead time and infra handshake. Can you share what your network posture is?
[02:20] Jamal Brooks: We're in a hybrid state. Primary workloads must stay within EU regions, ideally in our AWS account. VPC peering is preferred — peered endpoints or private link. We can accept egress rules but need to avoid public internet egress for token payloads.
[02:36] Diego Ramos: Got it. We support VPC peering and Private Link; we also offer Private self-hosted bundle if you need air-gapped deploys, but that's a different procurement path.
[02:45] Ayesha Khan: If possible, we'd prefer Redwood hosted with VPC peering for initial pilot — faster — then evaluate Dedicated later. Security-wise we need KMS integration, SAML SSO, and audit logs to our SIEM.

[03:20] Maya Chen: Makes sense. On SLA: what are your latency targets and acceptable error rates for the pilot?
[03:26] Sofia Ruiz: For conversational search the product goal is P95 < 450ms for 128 token responses, and 99.9% availability during business hours. Cost target is also important — we have a per-conversation cost budget.
[03:40] Liam O'Connor: And for summarization longer sequences — up to 1,024 tokens — P95 up to 1200ms is acceptable but we'd like to optimize.

[04:05] Diego Ramos: Okay. We can look at model variant recommendations: a faster quantized LLM for search (lower cost, lower latency) and a larger model for higher-quality summaries with fallback policies. We have recommendations in the Optimize toolkit.
[04:19] Sofia Ruiz: When you say fallback policies, you mean automatic routing to a cheaper model or...
[04:24] Diego Ramos: Sorry — fallback as in if latency SLOs are missed or capacity constrained, requests can route to a compatible variant or queued with an informative retry. We'll show you the rollout config in the Console.

[05:02] Ayesha Khan: Important for us: we cannot keep user PII outside EU. Does Redwood support region pinning and model pinning per-customer?
[05:12] Maya Chen: Yes — region pinning is supported. You can pin to eu-west-1 or other EU regions. Model pinning and rollout policies live in the same config layer. We'll include the region-residency docs in the security pack.

[06:00] Jamal Brooks: Network wise — what's the expected list of IP ranges to whitelist? We need an itemized set to send to our infra.
[06:07] Diego Ramos: We'll send the CIDR ranges for the peering endpoints. For pilot we can also provide short-lived certs if you prefer mTLS.
[06:15] Jamal Brooks: mTLS would be great. Avoids extra firewall fiddling.

[06:45] Maya Chen: On data handling — all inference payloads can be configured to not persist. We also support KV cache settings and prefix caching policies that can be disabled. Any retention requirements?
[06:58] Ayesha Khan: Minimal retention; we need logs forwarded to SIEM but payloads must not be stored beyond processing. Also want redaction support for certain fields.
[07:10] Diego Ramos: We have configurable redaction and structured output to remove PII before logging. We'll include examples in the runbook.

[08:00] Sofia Ruiz: Timeline — we want a 2-week pilot, starting mid-May, and decision by early June. Is that realistic?
[08:08] Maya Chen: Yes. If we start week of 2026-05-18 we can run 2 weeks of pilot, collect SLA metrics and a quality eval set, and then debrief.
[08:15] Liam O'Connor: We'll share a small evaluation prompt set — about 150 prompts for quality/regression checks. Diego, can you run them against candidate models?
[08:23] Diego Ramos: Yeah, we'll run them against the recommended variants and give latency/cost breakdowns and a quality summary.

[09:00] Jenna Patel: Admin note — I'll set up the pilot SOW and onboarding timeline in the project tracker and share access.
[09:06] Ayesha Khan: Great. Also — one more compliance item: we need evidence of penetration testing and retention of audit logs for 13 months.
[09:15] Maya Chen: We can provide the penetration test summary and confirm log retention options; Redwood Console has configurable retention and exports to S3 which you can attach to your SIEM.

[10:00] Diego Ramos: Quick technical deep-dive: latency is a function of model size, sequence length, and batching. For conversational search where latency matters, continuous batching windows are tuned aggressively; we can set smaller batching windows for low-latency but higher cost. We can also enable KV caching for repeated prefixes.
[10:22] Liam O'Connor: There's a trade-off then — smaller batches = higher cost. We need a suggested configuration that meets P95 < 450ms at our expected QPS.
[10:30] Diego Ramos: Exactly. For an expected pilot QPS of ~3 rps we can meet P95 with a quantized 7B variant in EU region with small batch thresholds. If QPS spikes you may want Dedicated capacity.

[11:05] Jamal Brooks: Do you have a recommended autoscaling/burst policy for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[11:11] Diego Ramos: For Dedicated, we recommend reserved pools sized for steady-state and burst for 2x. Hosted has adaptive pools and can fall back to compatible variants when capacity is low; we'll show how routing policies work in the Console.

[12:00] Ayesha Khan: About encryption — we require customer-managed keys for production. Is that supported for hosted?
[12:08] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood supports KMS integrations with customer-managed keys (CMKs) for both hosted and dedicated. We'll include the integration steps in the security pack; for Private deployments you can bring your own HSM too.

[13:10] Sofia Ruiz: On success criteria for pilot — to recap, we need: P95 < 450ms for search, error rate < 0.5%, and cost below X per 1k tokens (we'll define X in doc). Also quality regressions below a set threshold on your eval set.
[13:25] Liam O'Connor: We'll define quality thresholds and share them in a doc.

[14:00] Diego Ramos: For the evaluation, please include edge-case prompts and approximate token lengths so we'll run the right sequences. Also include any rate-limiting expected to simulate traffic.
[14:12] Sofia Ruiz: We'll include spikes in traffic to validate autoscaling.

[15:00] Maya Chen: A few practical items — we will need a technical point of contact (Jamal) and a legal/ procurement point for the SOW. Also we'll need to confirm billing account for pilot.
[15:12] Jamal Brooks: I'll be the TPOC for infra. Procurement is with Lauren in legal — we'll put her on the thread.

[16:00] Ayesha Khan: One risk: our legal team is strict on cross-border transfers — even with EU pinning they may ask for on-prem options. What's your expected lead time for Private/on-prem?
[16:15] Maya Chen: Private or on-prem typically takes longer — roughly 6-10 weeks depending on access and procurement. For pilot we recommend hosted with VPC peering to unblock product work; we can run the Private evaluation in parallel.

[17:00] Diego Ramos: I'll outline two paths in the pilot plan: fast path (hosted + VPC peering) and conservative path (Private/provisioning). Each path will have runbook steps and estimated timelines.

[18:00] Sofia Ruiz: Can you also include rollback and canary policies? We need to know how to mitigate quality regressions in release.
[18:08] Diego Ramos: Yes — canary deploys, A/B configs, and automatic fallback policies are supported; we'll attach example config snippets.

[19:20] Maya Chen: Regarding observability — you'll get per-route latency, token-level cost, and trace hooks. Any other telemetry needs?
[19:30] Jamal Brooks: We'd like distributed traces correlated with our request IDs; can you propagate trace headers?
[19:35] Diego Ramos: We support trace header propagation and can include examples. We also export traces to third-party APMs via exporter.

[20:00] Sofia Ruiz: One last product question — how do rollouts handle new model versions and quality regressions?
[20:10] Diego Ramos: The Console supports version pins, canary percentage, and automatic rollback thresholds tied to eval metrics. You can also tie alerts to quality regressions so the SE team gets notified.

[21:30] Ayesha Khan: Ok that sounds good. Budget question — do you offer a fixed-price pilot or usage-based?
[21:36] Maya Chen: We typically do a short-term usage-based pilot with a cap and then convert to reserved or committed monthly if you want Dedicated. We can also do a fixed-fee pilot SOW; we can propose both in the SOW.

[22:10] Sofia Ruiz: Please include pricing scenarios spelled out in the proposal.

[23:00] Diego Ramos: Technical checklist I will capture: network diagram, CIDR ranges, pilot prompt set, target QPS, eval metrics, and sample payloads.
[23:12] Jamal Brooks: We'll get that over by Friday.

[24:00] Jenna Patel: I'll create the project in Tracker and share access; I'll also send meeting notes and SOW draft.

[25:00] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to send security pack + SOC2 summary, CIDR/IP list for peering, pilot SOW with pricing scenarios, and Diego's benchmark plan. Customer to send network diagram, evaluation prompts, and success criteria. Pilot target start week of 2026-05-18.

[25:30] Ayesha Khan: Sounds good. Any blockers from Redwood's side?
[25:36] Maya Chen: None blocking — just waiting on items we discussed.

[26:00] Sofia Ruiz: We'll loop in procurement and legal once we have the SOW.

[40:00] (longer internal pause while notes are swapped)

[41:05] Diego Ramos: One small note — when you send logs to SIEM, we can stream audit logs via our export to your S3 and you can ingest from there; some customers prefer direct syslog but S3 is more reliable.
[41:20] Jamal Brooks: S3 export is fine. We'll give you the bucket transfer details later.

[42:00] Maya Chen: Final check: anyone need a follow-up deep technical session specifically on performance?
[42:08] Liam O'Connor: Yes please — a 60 minute SE deep dive on quantization and kernel selection would be helpful.
[42:15] Diego Ramos: I'll schedule that; propose next week after we get your prompt set.

[45:00] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll shoot over the security pack and SOW by Friday, and Diego will post the benchmark plan. Jenna will set the Tracker board and invite Lauren from procurement.
[45:20] Ayesha Khan: Great, thanks.
[45:25] Jenna Patel: Thanks all, bye.
[45:30] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker overlaps and acronyms may be imperfect (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache, "V-P-C" spelled out as VPC), some proper nouns may be transcribed incorrectly.
